Jewish Cemetery of Pesaro

Cemetery · Pesaro, Italy

Situated on a steep slope, the burial ground is made practicable by steps and walkways. In the upper part are the most ancient tombs, which are mostly cylindrical stelae or stones with inscriptions in Hebrew, sometimes carved with simple, elegant decorations. The style of the more recent part of the cemetery is completely different, testifying to the climate of emancipation that characterised the late 19th Century and the assimilation by the Jewish community of the customs of its host society. The tombs here, in fact, have a more monumental appearance and embody the typical elements of non-Jewish cemetery symbolism, such as broken columns, urns, lamps and torches. Guided visits are available.
